messages:
matt (sales): hey team, ACME POC just hit a blocker — they pinned to model `redwood-qa-7b-v2` but that variant isn't available in eu-west-1. customer is asking if we can backfill or provide a compatible variant for the demo tomorrow. :grimacing:
anya (solutions): ugh. do we know why that model isn't replicated? was it a region rollout or a deprecation?
ken (infra): looks like `redwood-qa-7b-v2` was never promoted to EU during the last replication pass. we have `redwood-qa-7b-v1` and `redwood-qa-7b-q4` in eu-west-1. v2 is on us-west-only at the moment.
sam (eng-runtime): compatibility-wise v1 is the closest, but there are a couple of tokenizer differences that may slightly change outputs. we can offer automatic fallback routing to `v1` with a note about potential minor drift.
matt (sales): client is sensitive about output parity — the POC eval suite will run exact-match tests. if we switch to v1, results could fail and wreck the trial. any other options?
anya (solutions): is cross-region pinning allowed for dedicated/private customers? they asked for eu data residency but for the demo they're OK with proxying if we can guarantee no logs leave region.
emily (security): we cannot stream logs outside the region for eu-residency customers. However, for a short demo we could do a temporary exception if KMS stays in eu-west and we sign an addendum. need legal + audit trail.
ken (infra): technical workaround: we can create a temporary model alias `redwood-qa-7b-eu-demo` that routes to `v2` hosted in us-west but with KV cache and telemetry disabled and all encryption using the customer's eu KMS. Latency will be higher (~200-400ms additional).
sam (eng-runtime): to add: if they pin by full model id (`redwood-qa-7b-v2`) aliasing won't help unless we create the alias and support model ID remapping in the POC config. that's doable but requires a short release and a DB migration for alias table. estimate ~3-4 hours ops + 1 hour QA.
matt (sales): pricing concern: client is worried about cross-region egress costs if we do the us-west route. are those charged to customer or absorbed?
\enya (sre-bot): [INFO] INC-4321 created — "ACME POC: region model mismatch & kms question". assigned to infra + eng-runtime.
ken (infra): pricing note — cross-region egress would be billed at standard rates to the customer unless we explicitly absorb it for the POC. if we absorb it, we should cap at a number and include in the POC terms.
matt (sales): ok propose two options to ACME: 1) quick alias + remap to allow exact model id for demo (latency + egress, 4hr ops), absorb egress up to $200 for the POC; 2) route them to `v1` in-region with a note about potential eval variance (instant). which should I propose?
anya (solutions): offer both. recommend option 1 as "premium" demo if they care about parity. include explicit note about KMS audit and latency.
emily (security): I'll pre-check the addendum language with legal. we can approve the alias route if KMS is configured to keep keys in eu-west and telemetry flags are off. need customer's KMS ARN.
sam (eng-runtime): I'll prep the alias remap patch and a rollback plan. tagging @ken for infra DB work.
ken (infra): ack. I'll reserve a maintenance window at 11:00 UTC and ping when done.
matt (sales): perfect — I'll message ACME with both options and ask for KMS ARN / approval for absorbing up to $200 egress. thanks all. :thumbsup:
anya (solutions): also add a one-off eval run to a shared bucket so they can see diff heatmap. helps with parity conversations.
matt (sales): good idea, include that in email. I'll update INC-4321 with customer's reply when it lands.
